Asset type: independent full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book XVIII, chapter 7, “The Different Kinds of Grain”
Primary request: Make one living harvest-and-threshing scene that clearly distinguishes Pliny’s two principal grain classes without becoming a specimen plate. Inside a modest circular packed-earth threshing floor, exactly three complete adult workers handle crops in different natural forms: one complete standing woman holds a complete bound sheaf showing long-bearded barley ears beside fuller wheat and hulled spelt; one complete kneeling man opens mature bean and chickpea pods into one broad unmarked wicker tray; one complete standing man uses one complete jointed wooden threshing flail on a low irregular layer of cereal ears. Behind the threshing floor, a complete rooted strip of wheat, barley and spelt transitions naturally into a separate complete rooted patch of branching beans and chickpeas with visible leaves and pods.
Scene/backdrop: one coherent early-Roman farm edge at harvest. The threshing floor has a low closed oval stone curb: the ENTIRE continuous oval perimeter must be visible, including its nearest lower arc, with a wide band of untouched earth or vellum outside the curb on the left, right, top and especially below. One small open granary shelter stands alone in the middle distance with its full roof, all four corners, all posts, open interior and ground contact visible and clear landscape space on every side. Add one modest winnowed grain mound and one separate modest pile of unopened legume pods inside the circle. No other building, market, mill, bread, birds or animals.
Style/medium: original Plinian natural-history folio on warm fibrous aged vellum with handmade irregularity; iron-gall contours, exceptionally fine cross-hatching, stipple and dry-brush abrasion; restrained umber, lampblack, muted verdigris, faded lapis, madder and ochre mineral pigments; ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough in material and polished in draftsmanship; crop-morphology dialect with precise awns, nodes, fibrous roots glimpsed at one lifted clod, branching pod stems, ochre chaff movement and restrained green-brown leaf variation.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2, intended as a 1536x1024 preservation master; pull the viewpoint well back and slightly upward so the complete threshing-floor oval occupies no more than the middle two-thirds of the canvas and is surrounded by generous empty ground. Build a triangular rhythm between the complete cereal sheaf at left, low pod tray near center and moving flail at right; keep the small complete shelter near upper-center, never near an edge. Let a small sweep of chaff remain close to the flail. Keep all three complete people, every head, hand, finger, leg and foot, full sheaf, full tray and all pods, entire jointed flail including both wooden members and connector, complete closed threshing-floor curb, both working piles, every featured rooted plant from ground contact to highest ear or pod, complete shelter, fields and hills wholly within generous blank vellum margins. One harvest moment only, never a botanical chart, labelled catalogue, grid, panel, collage, cross-section, timeline or repeated frame.
Lighting/mood: dry clear harvest morning; abundance, close observation, practiced knowledge and tactile order.
Color palette: warm vellum, iron-gall umber and lampblack, pale and deep ochre grain and chaff, muted verdigris bean/chickpea foliage, faded-lapis distance, restrained madder garments.
Materials/textures: fibrous vellum, packed earth, low stone curb, wheat/spelt/barley ears and awns, straw, fibrous roots, bean/chickpea leaves and pods, loose grain, woven tray, worn flail wood and rough wool.
Historical and botanical framing: faithfully evoke the chapter’s distinction between cereals and leguminous crops, including ears versus pods and differing stalk/leaf habits, while treating Pliny’s timings and regional claims as historical natural-history observations rather than modern agronomic certainty.
Constraints: exactly three complete adult people; exactly one complete jointed flail, one complete wicker tray, one complete small open granary shelter, one fully closed and wholly visible threshing-floor curb; recognizable plausible wheat, barley, spelt, bean and chickpea morphology; natural anatomy and rooted vegetation; opaque RGB/sRGB.
Avoid: any part of the threshing-floor curb or shelter touching or crossing an image edge; lettering, captions, labels, numerals, pseudo-writing, inscriptions, signatures, logos, watermarks, sacks, scales, scrolls, tablets, maize/corn cobs, rice paddies, sunflower, extra people, children, animals, birds, bakery, market, floating seeds, plants aligned as specimens, equal rectangular crop plots, cutaway, photography, photorealism, glossy CGI, frames, grids, panels, split scenes, repeated panels, multiple identical frames, cropped people, flail, sheaf, tray, plants, roots, piles, threshing circle, shelter, field or hills.
Output intent: one unified opaque landscape illustration, 3:2 composition, no transparency and no text-like marks anywhere.
chapters.visualQaNotes: Accepted after two framing rejections and a targeted independent regeneration, then inspected at original resolution. Exactly three complete workers handle cereal ears and legume pods on one complete closed threshing-floor oval; the complete jointed flail, sheaf, tray, grain mound, rooted wheat/barley/spelt and bean/chickpea patches, freestanding shelter, fields and hills remain fully contained. No text, pseudo-writing, specimen grid, extra figure or animal, panel, repeated frame, crop or anatomy failure was observed.
